observation.visible_scene: A low, close view of a small rocky stream. In the center a short cascade of white, aerated water tumbles through a gap between rounded boulders and splashes into a shallow, murky tan pool. Large gray and moss-green stones frame the upper and right edges, and a smooth yellowish stone sits at the far right. Submerged rounded stones are visible through the brownish foreground water, with bright highlights moving across the surface.
visible_changes: The white frothy cascade churns continuously: the foam patch stays centered but its shape, splashes and bubble clusters change from frame to frame.
Ripples and moving specular highlights propagate across the pool surface, especially in the foreground, indicating ongoing water motion.
Bubbles and small foam patches appear, drift briefly, and vanish near the base of the cascade and on the pool surface.
The arrangement of rocks (left gray boulder, top dark boulder, right green mossy boulder, far-right yellow stone) remains fixed throughout, with no object translation.
The foreground water color and the submerged stones stay persistent; only the surface texture and reflections shift.
outside_clip_unknowns: The upstream source feeding the cascade and the downstream path of the flow are outside the frame.
Whether the water rate changes over a longer timescale is unknown within this 2.7-second excerpt.
uncertain_details: Camera motion: the static rock positions suggest a fixed camera, but very slight handheld drift cannot be ruled out.
The bright shapes in the foreground are partly surface reflections and partly submerged stones seen through water; distinguishing the two frame-by-frame is uncertain.
The cascade is already in full flow at the first frame and still flowing at the last; no onset or completion is captured.
